findings.finding: The plan states the new claim check goes into the claims registry, but notes `iterate_checks.py` is "at its cap" without any change listed to raise or restructure that cap. If the registry genuinely enforces a limit, registration is a blocker; if the cap is a soft convention, the plan should say which.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit step to either raise the cap, or document that the cap refers to something else (e.g., a review-complexity threshold) and how registration works around it. This is the one item that could make the whole unit unimplementable as written.

findings.finding: Path classification lives in `affected_acs_gate.py` (pure rule), but `affected_acs_replay.py` must classify historical events the same way. The plan doesn't say the replay imports the gate's classifier; if it re-implements or (worse) interprets historical paths differently, the replay measurement and the live check will disagree, and the acceptance criterion ("replay over the 100-PR window") becomes ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly that replay uses the gate's classification function, and that a historical event failing under today's rules is reported as a pre-existing gap, not a new failure.

findings.finding: The replay over "the last N recorded iterate events" must have a defined pass condition. Is the acceptance criterion "all 100 events have `affected_acs`" (almost certainly fails — the whole premise is 11 of 17 behaviour-adding PRs left no AC behind) or "all events that would require a declaration under the new gate have one"? The plan doesn't say, and the campaign-halt rule ("stop the campaign if a measure fails") makes this load-bearing.
findings.suggestion: Define the replay's done-when precisely: which events count as runtime-touching, and whether historical non-compliance is a baseline measurement (expected) or a failure.

findings.finding: Presence-only declaration test ("never reads content") means an iterate can satisfy the gate with `affected_acs: "none"` while actually changing runtime code. That's an accepted scope cut for P1, but worth noting the blind-SKIP path plus presence-only means the check can't catch wrong declarations at all.
findings.suggestion: Fine for this unit — but record it as a known limitation in F5b.md so a later unit can tighten it, and make sure the SKIP case is logged visibly so silent skips don't look like passes.

findings.finding: Renames/moves of runtime files (e.g., moving a file from `shared/` to `docs/`, or a plugin reorganization) will require declarations under the path rule even when behaviour is unchanged. This may generate friction and habituate `affected_acs: checked, unchanged` boilerplate, diluting the signal.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable, but mention the "checked-and-left-unchanged" reason string in F5b.md examples so authors have a sanctioned low-effort truthful answer.

findings.finding: No real exposure — the gate is a local script over repo paths and event extras, read-only replay. Nothing here handles untrusted input beyond repo contents.

The requirement covers all runtime-touching iterates, but `requires_declaration` additionally restricts enforcement to `feature/change/bug`. A runtime-changing refactor or another iterate type could escape the requirement.
findings.suggestion: Make runtime changes the deciding condition, unless P1 explicitly authorizes those type exclusions. Test a runtime-touching iterate outside those three types.

findings.finding: The plan does not establish how F11 sees the declaration that will appear in `work_completed`. If F11 runs before that event is written, checking recorded events can inspect stale data or SKIP the fresh iterate. With no write-time gate, this connection is essential.
findings.suggestion: Specify the declaration source and lifecycle ordering. Add an integration test proving that a fresh runtime iterate fails without the field, passes with it, and persists that same declaration in its completion event. Missing required evidence must not count as successful validation.

findings.finding: “Last N recorded iterate events” does not necessarily reproduce the required 100-PR window. PRs can contain multiple iterates, and missing historical path evidence could cause SKIPs that make coverage appear complete.
findings.suggestion: Anchor replay to the specified PR window, associate its completion events, and report eligible, declared, missing, and unclassifiable counts separately. Test that incomplete evidence cannot produce a passing measurement, and explicitly stop for the operator when the measure fails.  The shared pure rule and read-only replay are a reasonable, restrained design. Resolve eligibility coverage, F11 lifecycle integration, and replay measurement semantics before implementation is accepted.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

doubt.disposition: Stage 3 applies only to migrations, async or concurrency, cross-plugin imports and irreversible operations; none touched here

findings.finding: The check never filters on `source == "iterate"`. `_work_event` matches any `work_completed` event whose `adr_id` equals the run id; a build/campaign run with `intent: change` and runtime-touching paths would be FAILED by this gate, even though the spec and the replay tool scope the rule to iterate events only (`replay` filters `source == "iterate"`). The check and the replay can disagree on the same event.
findings.suggestion: In `_work_event` or the check, require `evt.get("source") == "iterate"` before applying the intent filter, matching the replay tool and the spec's "feature/change/bug iterate" scope.

findings.finding: Historical iterate events that lack `changed_files` are silently dropped (`files if isinstance(files, list) else []` → `requires_declaration` false → not counted as `required`). The acceptance criterion is "replay over the 100-PR window shows the field required on all runtime-touching iterates" — events without recorded paths are runtime-touching-unknown, not non-runtime, and the replay has no git-view fallback, so `required` undercounts and old missing declarations are invisible. The F11 check itself treats this state as BLIND; the replay should surface it (e.g., a `blind` count) rather than skip.
findings.suggestion: Count events with no `changed_files` (and a runtime-intent) separately as `blind`/`unknown` in the replay output so the measure is honest.

findings.finding: When `git_context == "work_tree"` and `_iterate_changed_paths` returns an empty list (e.g., a branch already merged, or a commit hash that resolves to nothing), `paths` is `[]` (not `None`), so the `changed_files` fallback on the event is skipped and the check reports "no runtime path touched" — reading blindness as clean for the event-supplied path list. The spec's stance is "a blind branch view SKIPPED", not pass-as-clean.
findings.suggestion: Only use the git-view result when it is `None`-vs-list distinguishable; if the git view yields an empty list but the event lists runtime `changed_files`, prefer the event list (or report BLIND).

findings.finding: The skip-path assertions compare `severity == "skipped"` but never assert `ok`; more importantly there is no test that the check rejects a `source: "build"` event (which, per the finding above, it currently wouldn't skip) and no test of the empty-git-view + event-`changed_files` interaction. A regression in either direction would pass the suite.
findings.suggestion: Add cases: a `work_completed` event with `source: "build"`, intent `change`, runtime paths → expect SKIPPED; and a work-tree scenario where the git view is empty but `changed_files` lists a runtime path.  Overall: the core rule (presence-only gate) is implemented and reasonably tested, but the check's missing `source == "iterate"` filter and the replay's silent drop of path-less events are real scope/measure defects against the acceptance criteria. Ship-with-fixes.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: Events with missing or malformed `changed_files` are treated as having no runtime changes and silently excluded from `required`. Consequently, a 100-event window with unavailable path data can report `required: 0, missing: 0`, without establishing the acceptance criterion. The live verifier explicitly distinguishes this state as blind; replay loses that distinction.
findings.suggestion: Report unknown path coverage separately and mark the measurement inconclusive when it exists, or reconstruct those events’ changed paths from Git. Add a test showing that unavailable path data cannot produce an apparently clean measurement.  Ship-with-fixes: the replay needs to distinguish unknown coverage from confirmed non-runtime changes. This review is limited to the supplied diff: environment policy blocked repository reads and test execution, so I could not verify the binding brief or the fresh-iterate F11 result.
